title: Phones & syncing
blurb: Work email on a phone, photos to the computer, Phone Link, iPhone and Android.

remedies.title: Set up work email on my phone
remedies.why: Most workplaces want the Outlook app (and sometimes the Company Portal or Authenticator) on phones.

steps.text: Install Microsoft Outlook from the App Store / Google Play and add your work address.
Approve the sign-in in Microsoft Authenticator if asked.
If it asks to install Company Portal or to protect work data, follow it; your workplace requires it.

remedies.escalate: If it says your device isn't allowed, IT has to approve it.

remedies.title: Copy photos from my phone to the computer
remedies.why: A cable import is fastest; cloud photo services do it automatically.

steps.text: iPhone: plug in, unlock the phone and tap Trust, then open the Photos app on the PC › Import.
Android: plug in, choose File transfer on the phone's USB notification, then open the phone in File Explorer › DCIM.
iPhone: plug in, Trust, then Photos or Image Capture › Import. Or AirDrop them.
Android: use Google Photos, or a USB cable with an Android file transfer app.
Automatic: iCloud Photos, Google Photos or OneDrive camera upload.

remedies.title: Computer doesn't see my phone over USB
remedies.why: The cable only charges, the phone is locked, or the phone hasn't trusted the computer.

steps.text: Unlock the phone; tap Trust (iPhone) or choose File transfer (Android) when asked.
Use the cable that came with the phone; many cheap cables only charge.
Try another USB port directly on the computer.
iPhone on Windows: install Apple Devices from the Microsoft Store.

remedies.title: Use my phone's texts and calls on the PC (Phone Link)
remedies.why: Phone Link connects an Android or iPhone to Windows for messages, calls and notifications.

steps.text: Open Phone Link from Start and follow the QR code to pair.
Keep Bluetooth on both devices; iPhone features are more limited.

remedies.title: AirDrop, Handoff or iPhone calls on the Mac don't work
remedies.why: Both devices need the same Apple Account, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on, and Handoff allowed.

steps.text: Sign in with the same Apple Account on both; turn on Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
Turn on "Allow Handoff between this Mac and your iCloud devices" in General › AirDrop & Handoff.
AirDrop: set "Allow me to be discovered by" to Everyone for 10 Minutes on the receiving device.
